newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CONTINUE PROBE INTO COPPER "CACHE".
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CONTINUE PROBE INTO COPPER "CACHE".

text.p: The Dutch Statistical Office said on Tuesday it was continuing to investigate import and export data it gave to the World Bureau of Metals Statistics, which resulted in a controversial report on copper stocks.
"We're still looking at the data. There are still some programmes to run and we don't have any conclusion yet," a spokesman for the office (CBS) told Reuters.

The WBMS report threw the copper market into confusion last week, raising the possibility that over 500,000 tonnes of copper lay "hidden" in Rotterdam warehouses and had not been reported to the London Metal Exchange (LME).
Traders and analysts dismissed the WBMS report, saying it was impossible for such a large amount of copper to be lying unrecorded in the Netherlands.

Warehouse keepers in Rotterdam also denied the suggestions, saying a statistical discrepency may have arisen because Dutch official trade data included all copper coming into and leaving the country and not that purely destined for LME-nominated warehouses.
Copper prices rallied to five-month highs above $2,200 a tonne on Tuesday as official LME data showed another decline in world stocks, taking them to six-year lows below 100,000 tonnes.
